headline: High: Gemini CLI’s filesystem/MCP/network defaults create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks; godot_rl_agents adds little isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write repo files, use MCP, and process stdin/stdout, so attacker-controlled content in shared files or MCP outputs can be treated as instructions. godot_rl_agents has no documented protective channel or isolation, so the pair can be bridged through the filesystem rather than being provably blocked.
conditions: IF agent_b or a shared file writes attacker-controlled text into a directory Gemini CLI reads
IF Gemini CLI is configured to consume MCP server output from an untrusted server
mitigations: Restrict Gemini CLI to a dedicated working directory
Disable or whitelist MCP servers before running
Review any file-fed prompts before execution
Separate the two agents onto different filesystems
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for file and MCP inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment, and can egress broadly to Google APIs or user-configured MCP servers. godot_rl_agents documents no data classes or egress, so the main leakage path is Gemini CLI exporting shared workspace contents rather than a proven bidirectional leak.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace
IF Gemini CLI is allowed to send prompts or file contents to external APIs or MCP servers
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared directory
Run Gemini CLI in a separate workspace
Disable network egress for the session
Use a throwaway API key with minimal scope
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its concurrency model says shared state with other instances is via filesystem and git only. godot_rl_agents has no documented locking or write constraints, so concurrent access to the same repo can corrupt files or git state by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or working tree
IF either agent writes git state without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working trees
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
Avoid concurrent edits to shared files
requires-engineering: add file and git locks in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can generate code, shell actions, and MCP-driven outputs that another agent may treat as authoritative. godot_rl_agents is a simulation-oriented project with no documented verification layer, so if its outputs are consumed downstream, errors can propagate even though direct action authority is not shown.
conditions: IF outputs from Gemini CLI are copied into godot_rl_agents workflows without review
IF downstream automation treats either agent’s text as authoritative
mitigations: Require human review of generated outputs
Add a verification step before reuse
Keep simulation outputs separate from operational scripts
Log source provenance for copied text
requires-engineering: implement schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented for godot_rl_agents, while Gemini CLI handles Google-account/API-key mediated data and local files. The pair therefore shows only a limited compliance surface, with the main concern being accidental inclusion of regulated data in Gemini CLI’s workspace.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in Gemini CLI’s workspace
IF organizational policy forbids sending that data to Google-hosted services
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the workspace
Use non-sensitive test data only
Confirm retention settings for the Google account tier
Document a data-handling policy for the pair
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA or approved residency setup
